title: Make Naam the work of your life
subtitle: Raag Gauree · Ang 290
summary: The shabad begins by giving the saints a clear assignment — let Naam be the real work. It presses past distraction, calling for remembrance, shared encouragement, and the peace that even the drowning can find in the treasure of the Name.
whyItMatters: This one meets the person who is searching hard, exhausted, and still unconvinced that rest is possible. Taken seriously, it gathers scattered effort into one practice and turns private seeking into a shared, living discipline.
takeaway: Let Naam become the work that orders everything else.

lines.translation: O friends, O Saints, make this your work.
Renounce everything else, and chant the Name of the Lord.
Meditate, meditate, meditate in remembrance of Him, and find peace.
Chant the Naam yourself, and inspire others to chant it.
By loving devotional worship, you shall cross over the world-ocean.
Without devotional meditation, the body will be just ashes.
All joys and comforts are in the treasure of the Naam.
Even the drowning can reach the place of rest and safety.
O Nanak, chant the Naam, the treasure of excellence. ||5||

structure: The shabad names the central task without hesitation: chant the Lord's Name.
From there it says to practice it personally and help others into the same remembrance.
It finally promises rest, joy, and the ending of sorrow in the treasure of Naam.
